title: Defining a Relativity-Proof Notion of the Present via Spatio-temporal Indeterminism
version: Version of record, published online 14 June 2019; Foundations of Physics 50 (2020) 644–664; open access CC-BY 4.0; DOI 10.1007/s10701-019-00267-x.
locator: Read in full from the publisher OA PDF (local copy /private/tmp/opencode/muller2019-present.pdf, 21 pages). Hinge material: §2.2–2.3 (BT, Defs. 1–5, Facts 1–2; 'consecutive choice points' passage p. 655); §3 (Defs. 6–12, pp. 657–658; fn. 23 omits Weiner's postulate 'to keep matters simple'); §4 (Fact 4 and Theorem 1, pp. 661–662; featureless clause p. 661; fn. 26 identity condition); Figs. 5–6; §5 closing suggestion p. 662.
assumptions: Written hypothesis class only: Definition 6 BST structure = dense, no maxima/minima, infima for lower-bounded chains, suprema-in-h for upper-bounded chains, prior choice principle (chain form); Weiner's postulate explicitly omitted (fn. 23); sole exclusion is the two-clause 'featureless' definition (p. 661).
conclusion: Theorem 1 (pp. 661–662) asserts that ∼|h is neither the identity nor the universal relation for every history h of a non-featureless BST structure, defined wholly in relativistically sound BST notions; §2.3 characterizes co-presentness regions as intervals between consecutive choice points; no proof of Theorem 1 is given in the paper (it follows two finite illustrations, Figs. 5–6); fn. 26 offers 'every event a choice point and no modal correlations' as a sufficient condition for identity.
proof_status: Authors' statement inspected directly; no proof published. Independent clause-by-clause audit (CANDIDATE.md §2, symbolic hand proofs, no numerical computation) finds a counterexample — the dense comb — satisfying every written Definition-6 clause plus Weiner's postulate, historical connection, and no-MFB, with choice points exactly ℚ, cll(t) = ℚ∩(−∞,t), and ∼|h_T = identity; Theorem 1 is therefore false as stated. Facts 1–4 are not contradicted in the comb (Fact 4's ⇐ direction and the identity (*) used in its proof verify directly).
relevance: Exact primary hinge of Route B: whether the published nontriviality claim survives its own written axioms.
limits: No erratum, comment, or correction found (bounded search; see rsb-openalex-muller2020-citations). No claim beyond the written Definition-6 hypothesis class; no claim against BST_NF (BMP 2021 Theorem 10.1), MBS/higher-dimensional spacetime, or objective becoming.

title: Branching space-time (postprint of the 1992 paper)
version: Postprint of 'Branching space-time', Synthese 92 (1992) 385–434; PhilSci-Archive p1003 (archival reference confirmed in BMP 2021 bibliography, p. 422, as Belnap 2003b).
locator: Read in full (local copy /private/tmp/opencode/belnap1992-postprint.pdf, 51 pages). Postulate set verified: 2-1 (partial order), 4-1 (no maxima), 6-1 (density), 7-1 (prior choice, chain form), 13-1 (prior choice principle), 13-5/13-6/13-8 (PCP variants, historical connection); Facts 13-11/13-12 (density + infima vs. ≡) and 13-15 ('yes and no').
assumptions: Postprint postulate set as written; no featureless clause and no co-presentness theory (the postprint predates that project).
conclusion: Supplies the full postulate set under which the comb is checked; nothing in it excludes a BST92 structure with densely many choice points on a shared trunk (no clause forbids choice-dense histories or non-isolated choice events).
proof_status: Postulates read directly and re-checked clause by clause against the comb (CANDIDATE.md §2); the comb satisfies 2-1, 4-1, 6-1, 7-1, 13-1 (chain PCP), 13-5, 13-6, 13-8.
relevance: Fixes the axiom set the counterexample must satisfy beyond Müller 2020's Definition 6; confirms no hidden postulate blocks the comb.
limits: Postprint predates and says nothing about co-presentness; no bearing on BST_NF or higher-dimensional spacetime.

title: Probability Theory and Causation: A Branching Space-Times Analysis
version: Version of record; The British Journal for the Philosophy of Science 56 (3) (2005) 487–520; DOI 10.1093/bjps/axi132 (Crossref-verified; printed pagination 487–520 confirmed in the PDF).
locator: Read in full (local copy /private/tmp/opencode/muller2005-probability.pdf, printed pp. 487–520). Postulate 4 (Weiner: suprema retain their order across histories) p. 513 with fn. 13 (formulation due to Weiner [1997], 'Probability in Branching Space Time', unpublished, University of Pittsburgh; the Appendix A model derived independently, emphasising 'radically non-isomorphic' histories); Definition 5 (primary space-like related modal funny business) p. 493; Postulate 1 (no MFB) p. 495; Appendix A 'Preservation of the ordering of suprema' pp. 516–518 (Postulate 4 not a consequence of the other BST postulates); Appendix B Definition 21 (BST+S) pp. 518–519 with Lemma 9, Corollary 1, and the closing fact that not every BST model extends to a BST+S model.
assumptions: Weiner's postulate as stated: for initial chains I, J contained in both histories, the order (equality/</>) of their history-relative suprema is preserved across h1, h2; BST92 postulates plus no-MFB (Postulate 1) for the probability-theoretic results; BST+S adds an equivalence relation of space-time points respecting the ordering.
conclusion: Weiner's postulate is independent of the remaining BST postulates (Appendix A countermodel); BST+S entails Postulate 4 (Corollary 1); some BST models admit no BST+S extension.
proof_status: Read directly. The dense comb is verified by hand to satisfy Postulate 4 (CANDIDATE.md §2: for I, J ⊆ (−∞,q]_T the suprema in h_T and in h_q coincide as reals ≤ q); whether the comb admits a BST+S strengthening is consistency-checked only and flagged not fully audited.
relevance: Source of Weiner's postulate, which the comb satisfies — showing the counterexample is not blocked by the location postulate the 2020 paper omits; and source of the BST+S definition used for the location-route scope check.
limits: BST+S admission of the comb not fully audited (open item, CANDIDATE.md §11.4); the probability-theoretic chapters are not otherwise load-bearing for the counterexample.

title: Branching Space-Times: Theory and Applications
version: Oxford University Press, Oxford Studies in Philosophy of Science; print edition © OUP 2022; ISBN 9780190884314 (hardback), 9780190884338 (epub); LCCN 2021033975; chapter DOIs 10.1093/oso/9780190884314.003.000N (url points to ch. 10); project shorthand 'BMP 2021'. Read via the open-access ruj.uj.edu.pl mirror (local copy /private/tmp/opencode/bmp2021-monograph.pdf, 445 pages, OUP corrected proof).
locator: Chs. 1–3 (pp. 3–76) and ch. 10 (pp. 342–385) read in full; Preface p. xiii states 'Chapter 10 integrates material from Müller (2006, 2019) and from Placek (2021)'. Key locators verified page-by-page: Postulate 2.6 (Weiner's postulate) p. 38; Definition 2.9 (space-time locations) p. 39; Definition 2.10 (common BST structure) p. 40; Definition 3.4 (PCP92) p. 51; Definition 3.11 (choice set) p. 61; Definition 3.15 (BST_NF structure) p. 62; Fact 3.17 (no choice points in BST_NF) p. 64; ch. 10: Definition 10.1 (desiderata D1–D6) p. 353; Fact 10.1 (CPC(e1,e2) iff H_e1 = H_e2) pp. 356–357; Definition 10.4 (featureless) p. 359; Theorem 10.1 with proof p. 359; Definition 10.9 (sticky MFB) p. 375.
assumptions: Ch. 10 works in BST_NF (choice sets, no choice points); co-presentness CPC is defined via identity of causae causantes and characterized by sameness of containing-history sets (Fact 10.1); featurelessness carries the same two clauses as Müller 2020 (Definition 10.4: (i) single history, or (ii) a history consisting wholly of elements of uncorrelated choice sets).
conclusion: The monograph restates the nontriviality result as Theorem 10.1 for BST_NF: in a non-featureless BST_NF structure, CP_C|h is neither the identity nor the universal relation on any history h. It never states that Müller 2019's Theorem 1 is false under the BST92/Definition-6 hypothesis class, contains no comb or dense-choice counterexample (chs. 1–3, 10), and its Theorem 10.1 proof's identity-triviality step ('This is only possible in a BST_NF structure in which each element of h is a member of an uncorrelated choice set', p. 359) is exactly where BST92 structures escape: in BST92 a non-choice event can differ in H_e from every other event without lying in any nontrivial choice set.
proof_status: Authors' proof read and its transfer to BST92 diagnosed (it fails). Rescope necessity verified independently: the BST_NF analogue of the comb (branch events doubled into choice sets c̈_t = {t_x : x ∈ {T} ∪ ℚ_≥t}) is a BST_NF structure (Definition 2.10 plus PCP_NF verified), but every trunk event then lies in a nontrivial choice set, so h_T is featureless under Definition 10.4(ii) and Theorem 10.1 is not violated (CANDIDATE.md §3).
relevance: Strongest rival: the silent rescope to BST_NF is exactly what blocks the comb; the Preface confirms ch. 10 was built from Müller (2006, 2019) without flagging the 2019 statement as false — evidence the rescope was not advertised as a correction.
limits: Chs. 4–9 not read; print copyright year (© 2022) vs. project shorthand 'BMP 2021' is a bibliographic variant only (LC record says [2020]; chapter DOIs and ISBN verified).

title: Past, present and future modally introduced
version: Online first 1 July 2019; version of record Synthese 198 (4) (2021) 3603–3624; DOI 10.1007/s11229-019-02302-w (Crossref-verified 2026-10-31). Note: CANDIDATE.md §7 refers to it as 'Placek 2019' after the online-first year; flagged for the reviewer — the version-of-record citation is Placek 2021, Synthese 198(4):3603–3624 (also listed in BMP 2021 bibliography, p. 426).
locator: Abstract and key excerpts defining his modal Present(e) (horizon-style); the paper is named in BMP 2021's Preface (p. xiii) as a source of ch. 10.
assumptions: A horizon-style modal present (Present(e)), not the CC-based co-presentness of Müller 2020 / BMP 2021 Definition 10.5.
conclusion: His degenerate 'single event' case corresponds to the all-events-chancy regime — the dual of the comb's dense-but-not-total chanciness; not a predecessor of the counterexample, but the nearest independently published instability observation.
proof_status: Abstract/excerpt level only; no claim about his proofs.
relevance: Nearest third predecessor at discovery depth for the novelty delta (CANDIDATE.md §7).
limits: Read depth insufficient for any claim beyond the degenerate-case observation; online-first (2019) vs. issue year (2021) is the only bibliographic uncertainty, now resolved.
